newsitem.title: UK: Latin American packaged food market grows.
newsitem.headline: Latin American packaged food market grows.

text.p: Latin American food diets are moving increasingly towards Western tastes and growing numbers of Latin Americans are shopping in supermarkets, a consumer market analyst group said on Friday.
Euromonitor said in a report that changing food habits had fuelled, among other things, growth in Latin America's packaged babyfood market.
"The Latin American diet is moving towards Western patterns, as ownership of refrigerators, microwave ovens and freezers becomes far more widespread," it said.
The packaged babyfood market has grown by 55.6 percent in volume terms since 1990 in Argentina, by 40 percent in Colombia and by 17 percent in Brazil.
Increasing numbers of supermarkets have boosted the growth in packaged food in Latin America, Euromonitor said in its report, "The Market for Packaged Foods in Latin America."
In Argentina, for instance, canned goods sales have grown by 24 percent since 1990 to $931 million in 1995.
This development has boosted local brands, as well as international brands like Nestle, Quaker, Kellogg's and RJR Nabisco, Euromonitor said.
In Brazil, the canned foods market has grown by 40 percent since 1990 to $1.2 billion in 1995, while frozen foods surged by 78.8 percent to $682.7 million.
But in Mexico, the economic crisis in 1995 hammered the packaged food business, with the canned foods market falling to $1.5 billion in 1995 from $2.4 billion in 1994.
Mexico's frozen foods market plummetted to $654.8 million in 1995 from $1.1 billion in 1994, Euromonitor said.
